newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dyke bursts in flood-hit eastern Germany.
newsitem.headline: Dyke bursts in flood-hit eastern Germany.

text.p: A dyke burst and water gushed into an area of eastern Germany on Wednesday after water levels in the region rose, a spokeswoman for local authorities said.

The spokeswoman said the dyke on the Oder River, which forms part of Germany's border with Poland, had been breached between the villages of Aurith and Brieskow-Finkenheerd and the area was filling up with water.
Officials had ordered the area to be evacuated on Tuesday.
Police were checking if all residents had obeyed the order, the spokeswoman said, and would force those who refused to leave their homes to leave.
Officials said they had also closed off large parts of the flood-hit region to reporters in the interests of their own safety.
Heavy flooding throughout the region over the last fortnight had already claimed more than 100 lives in the Czech Republic and Poland.
While Germany so far had escaped loss of life, hundreds of homes in the Oder region had already been flooded and towns had been hit by power cuts and overflowing sewers.
